content:
Tom: Our console just started returning 403 for project 'acme-pay' after we rotated a service account key. Org admin can't open project settings. Happened ~2026-03-16 18:12 UTC.
Maya: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact UI error and any request IDs?
Tom: UI shows '403 Permission Denied — You don't have access to this project'. UI trace id: ui-9f7a3. No other details in the popup.
deploy-bot: service-account-key-rotate event: sa-rot@acme rotated at 2026-03-16T18:11:54Z (audit id: aud-8812).
Maya: Ok, thanks. Do you know if the console access relies on the service account currently, or is it a human user who also lost access?
Tom: Both — our human org-admin and automation that uses the service account can't access the project UI. API calls by the automation also start returning 403 after the rotation.
Leo: Pinging @Elena from IAM to check audit/token logs.
Elena: I pulled the audit trail: we see `service_account.key.rotate` by system_user@acme at 18:11:54, followed by several token-exchange requests at 18:11:56-18:12:05. The exchange responses show delegated tokens but the `scopes` claim is missing the project console scope (`console:project:access`). Looks like scope trimming during exchange.
Maya: That's consistent with a scope-sanitization regression we've seen in canary. Tom — can you reproduce locally or share a failing cURL for the automation?
Tom: Repro: after rotating the key we call our token-exchange endpoint:
```
POST https://auth.redwood/api/v1/exchange
{ "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange", "subject_token": "<sa-token>", "requested_scopes": "console:read projects:acme-pay" }
```
Response is 200 with a JWT that decodes to claims missing `projects` and only has `scopes:["api:read"]`.
Leo: Quick workaround — grant the service account an explicit project role so ACLs don't solely rely on exchanged scopes. You can run:
```
POST /v1/orgs/acme/projects/acme-pay/roles/grant
{"member":"serviceAccount:sa-rot@acme","role":"project-admin"}
```
That should allow immediate access while we debug exchange.
Tom: Applied the grant, got 200 OK, but console still shows 403 for the automation. Human admin regained access after re-login though.
Elena: That points to session caching on the UI side — the browser session needs to pick up new bindings. Did the automation re-request a token after the grant?
Tom: Automation fetches a token on startup; it used the exchanged token (still missing projects). We forced a token refresh and now API calls succeed. Console remains 403 in headless automation render.
Maya: For the headless UI, the automation likely caches a session cookie. Try invalidating sessions: `POST /v1/sessions/invalidate?org=acme` or have the automation clear cookies and re-auth.
Tom: Invalidated sessions and restarted the automation — console access fixed. Good.
Elena: Root cause: token-exchange was dropping custom project-scopes during service account key rotation. Repro steps documented. I'll file a bug: ENG-iam #3421 — ensure token-exchange preserves `projects` and `console:*` scopes when rotating SA keys.
Leo: I've attached the relevant traces (trace id trace-54b2) and the exchange logs from 18:11:56-18:12:05 to the ticket. Short-term mitigation: add an automatic re-grant job to reapply project bindings after rotation and update runbooks to invalidate sessions post-rotation.
Maya: Escalating to the Dedicated IAM sprint and adding a postmortem task. @Elena please include regression test that exercises key rotation + token-exchange. :thumbsup:
Tom: Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. Please CC me on the PR and postmortem.
Maya: Will do. Follow-ups: ETA for fix? Elena: I'll prioritize a patch this week and put a rollback/patch plan in the ticket.
Tom: Good — closing on our side once we see the PR.
Maya: Marking as escalated and moving to #eng-iam and #eng-sre channels for triage.
